A simpler way to plan

Build a degree path.
One decision at a time.

You don’t need to understand every transfer policy before you begin. Start with your goal; build a clearer picture as you go.

Build my plan →
01

Start with your situation.

Tell us whether you’re exploring, already know your school or degree, or want to use learning you’ve completed. Choose your subject, study format, military connection, and the priority that matters most: speed, cost, transfer, or balance.

If you know your exact target, we keep it. If we haven’t mapped it, you’ll see an honest outline and the research still needed.

02

Upload your courses together.

Upload your transcript PDF, an Excel file, or our labeled CSV template. Review and edit your courses in one table, then add them together. You can start without records and return later.

Original course facts stay separate from a school’s transfer award. Saved interests, courses you are taking, and completed courses keep their own progress labels.

03

Compare a proposed route.

Where a course map is available, the worksheet brings degree requirements, outside options, proposed choices, and remaining university work together. Compare providers and what-if scenarios without losing your existing learning.

Where research is incomplete, the plan identifies gaps instead of inventing a course allocation. Current prices, pace, course availability, and school rules need to be added before a reliable finish estimate is possible.

04

Confirm, then move forward.

Your portal shows the current next task. Review the draft, send it to your school, and ask for written course approvals and an official credit evaluation. Sending the plan means waiting for review—not automatic approval.

Track progress and update the plan as you finish work. Community feedback can add useful evidence along the way, while your own school decisions remain the authority.
